output.summary: KEP-2578 proposes a Windows operational readiness standard for Kubernetes clusters that support Windows, defined in terms of existing Ginkgo tags and e2e tests, with a possible Sonobuoy-based certification bundle. The KEP is implementable at alpha stage.
output.rationale: The 1000s of existing Ginkgo tests do not give a clear meaning for Windows operational readiness, and Windows clusters vary in CNI, CRI and configuration, so users get a less stable experience than on Linux. The KEP defines readiness categories (core versus feature-specific), maps them to existing tags, and avoids new tooling in Kubernetes core. During PRR review, the approver noted the KEP is about building a test suite rather than a feature present in a running cluster, so PRR answers were not required.

alternatives.option: Define a new set of Ginkgo tags for Windows conformance
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says tags 'can be subject to change over time', so it does not couple the definition of Windows operational readiness to them; tags remain the canonical implementation detail only.

alternatives.option: Treat the standard as Windows Conformance with a Conformance specification
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers objected that there should not be a 'Conformance' specification, so it was framed as an operational readiness specification instead.

alternatives.option: Standardize on specific Windows versions 1909 and 2004 (SAC)
alternatives.why_not: A reviewer argued only LTSC versions (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) should be covered, since SAC versions were ending service; the discussion records a plan to push updates to the two latest SACs and latest LTS.

evidence.quote: Ginkgo tags, which are commonly used to define test suites, can be subject to change over time (either in their implementation, their definition, or both)
defines how these conformance tests can be run using *existing* Kubernetes ginkgo tags, without any additional tooling
This KEP appears to be about building a test suite as opposed to a feature that is enabled and always present inside of a running cluster.
the feedback was that there shouldnt be a "Conformance" Specification - hence we defined this as an operational readiness specification
I believe we should only be performing conformance tests on what would be officially supported at the time of 1.23, which would be LTSC versions of Windows Server
